item.title: Strong and shallow M6.0 earthquake hits Volcano Islands, Japan region
item.description: A strong earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 struck the Volcano Islands, Japan region at 03:55 UTC on March 2, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 20 km (12.4 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source

item.title: Winter weather impacts Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic while severe storm risk expands across parts of Oklahoma and Kansas
item.description: A lifting frontal boundary draped from the southern Plains to the Mid-Atlantic is producing a swath of mixed winter precipitation across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys on March 2, 2026, while setting the stage for isolated severe thunderstorms in Oklahoma and Kansas on March 3. Winter weather advisories are in effect from Indiana to Pennsylvania, with ice accretion possible across the higher terrain of the Appalachians, according to the Weather Prediction Center. Source

item.title: Continuous eruption at Ambae sends ash to 4 300 m (14 000 feet), Alert Level 3 maintained, Vanuatu
item.description: Volcanic ash from Ambae volcano, Vanuatu, was reported at 4 300 m (14 000 feet) above sea level on March 1, 2026. Authorities keep the volcano at Alert Level 3, with activity confined to the summit caldera and hazards limited to a 3 km (1.9 miles) exclusion zone. The ash cloud was observed moving southeast at approximately 28 km/h (17 mph). Source

item.title: Strong M6.1 earthquake hits near Simeulue, Indonesia
item.description: A strong and shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.1 hit near Simeulue, Indonesia, at 04:56 UTC (11:56 local time) on March 3, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 26.2 km (16 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source

item.title: Live watch: Blood moon total lunar eclipse of March 3, 2026
item.description: A blood moon total lunar eclipse occurring on March 3, 2026, will peak at 10:57 UTC, after the Moon enters totality at 10:29 UTC and remains fully immersed in Earth’s shadow for approximately 56 minutes. The event will be visible from much of Asia and Oceania, with live streams providing real-time views as totality unfolds. Source

item.title: Destructive cold lahar at Mount Merapi sweeps away vehicles following heavy rain, Indonesia
item.description: Heavy rainfall on March 3, 2026, triggered a destructive volcanic mudflow on Mount Merapi’s Kali Senowo channel in Magelang Regency, Central Java, Indonesia, sweeping away at least three trucks and one car. Source

item.title: Canada records lowest temperature in decades and record snowfall in winter 2025–26
item.description: Canada recorded its lowest temperature in decades during winter 2025–26, with −55.7°C (−68°F) measured at Braeburn, Yukon, on December 23. Seasonal snowfall reached 446 cm (176 inches) in Gander West, Newfoundland and Labrador, among the highest totals reported nationwide this winter, while Toronto registered its snowiest single day on record on January 25, when 46 cm (18 inches) fell at Toronto Pearson International Airport. item.title: Increased seismic activity recorded at Bulusan volcano, Philippines
item.description: A total of 49 volcanic earthquakes were recorded at Bulusan Volcano in Sorsogon Province, Philippines, between 03:00 LT on February 26 and 11:00 LT on March 2, 2026, prompting authorities to issue an advisory on increased seismic activity. Sixteen of the events were classified as volcano-tectonic earthquakes occurring at depths of 3--6 km (1.9--3.7 miles) beneath the northern and southeastern flanks of the volcano. item.title: Heavy snowfall across northern China triggers emergency responses
item.description: Northern China experienced widespread snowfall on March 1, 2026, with snow cover exceeding 250 000 km² (96 525 mi²) and a maximum snow depth of 23 cm (9 inches). The event prompted emergency responses across several provinces, including Hebei, Shanxi, and Gansu, according to official reports. Source

item.title: Two subtropical systems active simultaneously in South Atlantic, first such overlap documented in modern monitoring era
item.description: Subtropical Storm Caiobá formed off southern Brazil on March 2, 2026, after two subtropical depressions developed simultaneously in the South Atlantic. According to Metsul Meteorologia and available South Atlantic cyclone records, no previous instance of simultaneous subtropical depressions has been documented since formal monitoring and classification began. Caiobá moved away from the coast of Brazil without any major impacts. Source
